rationale: Upheld after exact genuine-version examination: printed page 67 contains one self-executing present-tense repeal of the November 15, 1905 appointment-authority order, dated January 12, 1906 and signed in print by Theodore Roosevelt. The complete source supports the exact first_end and whole_order_end date 1906-01-12 and the distinction between the exhausted repeal command and its continuing legal consequence. No future performance, wind-down, appointment action or later formal cleanup is required or evidenced.

clause_tests.inventory: One repeal sentence; signatures/date are authentication context. No independent prospective command, schedule, deadline or express savings. Body-only frozen quote faithfully matches the complete operative text.
clause_tests.effective_date: January 12, 1906: the dated instrument effects repeal in the operative present. No delayed-effective-date clause or future act condition.
clause_tests.first_cessation: The sole legal transition is accomplished on issuance, supporting task_completed on January 12, rather than assuming some unobserved later administrative performance. Continued cancellation of the target is a consequence.
clause_tests.earlier_candidates: November 15, 1905 is the target order date, not cessation of EO393; no cessation precedes EO393 issuance. No later formal disposition can be the first accomplishment of this immediately effected repeal.
clause_tests.cutoff: terminated / whole_order_status no is supported as absence of remaining executory force, not a finding that EO393 itself was formally revoked.

savings_residuals_test: Full page has no express savings or continuing independent EO393 duty. It does not itself direct removals, repayment or new appointments. Prior appointments and rights under other instruments are not adjudicated; no appointment performance is assumed. The completed repeal remains legally consequential without a surviving repeal task.
unresolved_material_gaps_assessment: No material missing performance evidence is needed for this self-executing transition. Broad historical-search coverage remains qualified as above; the card empty-gap list is not an assertion of omniscience.

rationale: Upheld for the exact date-limited scheduling scope. Printed page 76, dated September 20, 1906 and signed Theodore Roosevelt, President, permits the single ordinarily October 1 quarterly session to be held at the Governor office on November 15, 1906. That permission remains available on November 15; its first civil date with no fresh exercise is November 16. The card expressly identifies the equivalent close-of-November-15 boundary and does not find actual performance. Complete parent printed pages 33-36 show session continuation governed separately by the April 1, 1905 order, not a new independent continuing EO506 command.

clause_tests.inventory: One paragraph supplies one alternative date and specifies the Governor office for one quarterly session. No report, appointment, perpetual schedule, independent session-duration command or express savings is added. Frozen operative quote includes the complete paragraph.
clause_tests.effective_date: September 20, 1906 makes the prospective alternative available. It does not complete an unperformed meeting or exhaust the future permission on issuance.
clause_tests.first_cessation: expiration_by_own_terms at the close of November 15 inclusive; 1906-11-16 is the first civil date outside the authorized day. Date granularity is civil-day interpretation, not evidence of an observed administrative timestamp. The same-day exclusive reading would erase part or all of the expressly permitted day.
clause_tests.earlier_candidates: September 20 is issuance, not exhaustion; October 1 is the displaced ordinary date; the beginning of November 15 is the permitted day, not its termination. An earlier actual meeting, cancellation or intervening repeal is not established by inspected sources and is not inferred.
clause_tests.continuing_session: Parent printed page 33 states quarterly sessions continue as long as public business requires. EO506 changes one commencement date within that framework. A lawfully commenced session could therefore continue later; such continuation does not allow a fresh November-15 calendar exception on November 16 or add an independent EO506 duty. Neither convening nor adjournment is proved or assumed.
clause_tests.parent_scope: Read all parent printed pp33-36 through Roosevelt signature. Parent covers regular and special sessions, quorum, executive committee, departments, appointments, contracts, consulting engineers, reports and its own savings. EO506 neither reenacts those independent duties nor terminates the recurring schedule. Parent p36 preservation of consistent earlier Canal orders is a parent provision, not an EO506 savings clause.
clause_tests.cutoff: The one-day exception cannot supply fresh scheduling authority at the 2026 cutoff; terminated/no is supported for EO506 own operative scope, without adjudicating the parent whole lifecycle.

savings_residuals_test: No express EO506 savings on the complete page. Historical validity of the exception and acts of any lawfully held session may persist. Parent-governed continuation is expressly left intact; it is not silently counted as extinguished, and no continuing performance or duration is assumed.
unresolved_material_gaps_assessment: No actual convening/adjournment evidence is required to determine expiry of fresh permission by the specified date. The card reference to a local session-search.json is a producer search assertion only: that file was not opened and its no-intervening-change result is not independently certified here. No contrary earlier ending appears in the permitted examined pages; broad absence of intervening law is subject to the bounded-search qualification.
